issues.description: Public contract silently changed: empty-domain inputs now throw instead of returning NaN/undefined arrays
issues.detail: The prior implementation accepted any array (peek of empty returns undefined, arithmetic yields NaN). The new implementation throws. This strengthens the precondition of a published API — a classic LSP violation at the module boundary. Any caller relying on the old soft-fail behavior breaks. The contract change must be documented in release notes and the type signature, or made non-throwing for backwards compatibility.

issues.description: Parameter type `number[]` weaker than the actual precondition (NonEmptyArray)
issues.detail: The functions require non-empty domains at runtime but advertise `number[]` in the type signature. The contract is split between types and runtime checks. Since `peek` now has an overload for `readonly [T, ...T[]]`, the pan/zoom signatures should accept `NonEmptyArray<number>` (or `readonly [number, ...number[]]`) so the type system enforces what the body asserts. Otherwise the abstraction leaks.

issues.description: `coerceNumber` silently rewrites contract of `toNumber` by mapping null to 0
issues.detail: The original `panLinear` used `toNumber` (which can return null) as `lift`; arithmetic on null produced NaN. The new `coerceNumber` substitutes 0, changing observable output for non-numeric inputs. This is a weakening of postconditions — same inputs, different results — and is not covered by the PR description's claim of identical runtime behavior. Either preserve NaN propagation or document the new mapping.

issues.description: `Domain` return type `[number, number]` under-specifies invariants (ordering, finiteness)
issues.detail: The ADT for a domain typically carries invariants beyond `tuple of two numbers` — for example d0 <= d1, or both finite. The new `Domain` type captures arity but not these invariants. For an incremental typing PR this is acceptable, but worth a follow-up so callers cannot accidentally consume a [NaN, NaN] result as a valid domain.

issues.description: `peek` overload pair is correct but could be tightened to a single sound signature
issues.detail: The overloads form a sound contract: non-empty arrays guarantee T, others may yield undefined. This is a good ADT refinement. Minor note: prefer documenting the precondition in the JSDoc so callers reading types alone understand why one overload returns T unconditionally.

review.summary: The PR makes a reasonable first pass at typing pan/zoom, and the `peek` overloads are a clean ADT refinement. However, two contract changes slip in under the banner of "types only": empty domains now throw (strengthened precondition) and `coerceNumber` maps null to 0 instead of propagating NaN (weakened postcondition). Both are LSP-relevant at the public API boundary. The parameter types should also reflect the non-empty invariant the body now enforces, so the contract lives in the type system rather than as a runtime guard layered on a looser signature.
